messages:
maria-lopes: Heads-up — rewrap job kicked off last night and we saw a spike in KMS API errors + some gaps in audit logs. Anyone else seeing this? cc @kevin-choi @sophie

kevin-choi: I saw a burst of RequestLimitExceeded from AWS KMS around 03:12 UTC. The rewrap workers were parallelized across ~200 shards. We basically flooded the KMS regional QPS.

sophie: Are the audit events actually missing or just delayed? I noticed ~4% of objects didn't have a PutRecord in the audit sink on initial pass.

arnold: From the orchestration logs, retries were effectively aggressive — the backoff was disabled in the 2.1.0 worker roll. That explains the rapid retry storm.

jenna: Why was backoff disabled? I thought we needed speed for the backfills.

kms-orchestrator-bot: job rewrap-full-2026-11-05 started: total=1234567 objects, completed=0, started_by=maria-lopes

kevin-choi: Immediate mitigations I recommend: reduce parallelism to 32, enable jittered exponential backoff, implement per-key QPS limits, and add an audit-sync checkpoint so missing events get re-emitted instead of dropped.

maria-lopes: Agree. Also a RBAC point — current rewrap workers are granted broad kms:Encrypt/kms:Decrypt scopes across many customer keys. We should scope permissions to per-customer key policies for the sweep.

sophie: +1 on scoping. Also we should add a rewrap metadata header (e.g., rewrap-token + original-kid) to every envelope so downstream can reconcile and auditors can filter rewraps.

arnold: Quick patch for worker config below — will push to staging once we agree:

```yaml
rewrap:
  concurrency: 32
  batch_size: 100
  backoff:
    min_ms: 100
    max_ms: 20000
    factor: 2.0
    jitter: full
  per_key_qps: 10
  audit_checkpoint_interval: 60
```

jenna: Timeline? We can build and deploy the worker change to staging in ~45m, but the RBAC key policy change will need an infra ticket and key-admin approval.

maria-lopes: I'll open infra ticket and tag @kevin-choi for RBAC. Also we need to notify compliance about potential missing audit rows.

kevin-choi: created infra ticket INFRA-4839 https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-4839 — RBAC drafting + key policy change, assigning to security-ops for approval.

kms-orchestrator-bot: job rewrap-full-2026-11-05 progress update: completed=12345, errored=89, rate_limit_errors=73, last_error=RequestLimitExceeded

sophie: For error recovery: plan is to enqueue errored objects into a rewrap-retry queue with exponential backoff and a nondestructive marker (rewrap_attempts++). That way we can safely replay without losing audit linkage. Any objections?

arnold: Also recommend SLO gating: if provider 5xx or KMS rate errors >1% over a 10m window, scale workers down to zero (drain) and flip the cluster to read-only mode while we investigate.

maria-lopes: Action items from this thread:
1) patch worker config (concurrency/backoff/per-key qps) + rollback playbook
2) INFRA-4839 RBAC scoping and key-policy changes
3) audit re-emission job to backfill missing PutRecord events
4) SLO gating and drain automation
I'll schedule a 25-min incident sync in 15 minutes.

jenna: I'll own audit re-emission. arnold takes the worker patch. kevin owns RBAC/key-policy.

kevin-choi: noted — will need explicit key admin approval from security-ops before changing key policies.

sophie: small note — GCP KMS and Azure Key Vault have different per-project/per-tenant QPS limits and slightly different error semantics. We should add provider-specific throttle maps in runtime instead of a single global QPS cap.

maria-lopes: Good point. Add that to the retro: provider throttle mappings + unified audit schema + idempotent rewrap markers.

deploy-bot: canary for rewrap-worker:2.1.1 rolled out to staging

maria-lopes: Thanks all :thumbsup: We'll sync soon.
